answers.assumption_check: Assumed and to be measured by the proof: two boxes compile byte-identical lab files from the same charters (the observed diff on akiendell is only the charter fields runtime_role and gated_by, no host path), so committing the lab from any box merges cleanly. Not assumed: which step commits it; the build chooses between recompile_gate.sh committing its own output and a post-merge step, and the proof's teeth name the observable (git status clean, pull --ff-only succeeds), not the mechanism. Whether charters under skills/ are the only drifting sources is unmeasured; the proof recompiles over a scratch code root with a changed charter of any kind.
answers.builder_check: A Haiku builder needs and has: the writer (cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/recompile_gate.sh, env seams CAIRN_COMMONS_ROOT / CAIRN_CODE_ROOT / CAIRN_LAB_OUT / CAIRN_LOG_DIR for a scratch tree, per its own header); the door (the artifact/commit door, always `commit -- <paths>`, never a plain commit, per the repo rule); the proof location (cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/proofs/, red-first, one tooth per clause, PROVES declared); the existing sibling proofs to copy the scratch-tree setup from (test_recompile_gate.py, test_a_merge_recompiles_the_lab.py); and that the gate NEVER blocks its caller and always exits 0, so a failed commit is logged to the instance log, not raised. Windows cannot seal, so the Linux seal is the orchestrator's.
answers.children: none, because the fix is one gate's commit step and its proof: cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/recompile_gate.sh
answers.collision_check: No collision. CLAUDE.md's rule that the lab is derived, never authored allows several derived writers, and the gate committing its own regeneration is one of them; the lab being committed at all is deliberate (carried to a bare machine to regrow the system), which rules out gitignoring it. Law 5 says the thing and its story may not contradict: a stale committed lab contradicts its charters, which is the defect.
answers.falsifier_check: Falsifier: in a scratch commons plus code root, change a charter, run recompile_gate.sh, and the commons has a clean `git status` (tracked lab files committed) and a clone's `pull --ff-only` succeeds; on the unfixed gate the same sequence leaves modified lab files. Horizon: the next charter-changing merge on any box leaves the commons clean.
answers.gates_bound: proved (Law 8: a proof a hollow build could not pass, red on the unfixed gate) and feeds back to origin on failure (Law 3): the PROVEME crossing runs the proof under the tester's seal on Linux; a red returns the ticket to FIXME.
answers.missing_check: Nothing asserted-wrapped that is not: the failing state is measured (three skills lab files modified in the commons after charters a8d9ded2f and a61009024 added fields; git pull --ff-only aborted), and the producing path is read (recompile_gate.sh pokes the copy door on merge and on /sorted write-through; nothing commits the result). Open and carried into the build: a failed commit must be recorded (Law 7), and a box with no commit rights must not lose its compile.
answers.questions: none, because the mechanism is a CC-answerable hypothesis the proof measures, and the lab being tracked is settled at cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/recompile_gate.sh and its charter cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/intention+why.json
answers.title: a charter change and its compiled lab copy reach the commons together, so the lab never sits as uncommitted dirt that aborts a pull

bullets.text: The lab drifts after a charter change because recompile_gate.sh regenerates it into the working tree and nothing commits it; the next commons pull --ff-only on that box aborts. It bites every box, measured on akiendell 2026-11-19 with three skills charters.
Mechanism (gate commits its own output) is a hypothesis; the byte-identical-across-boxes tooth measures it, not Akien.
